content: A funeral home, also known as a mortuary, is a business that provides services related to the burial and funeral of deceased individuals, catering to the needs of both the deceased and their families. These services often include organizing a wake, conducting a funeral ceremony, and offering a chapel for the service. Funeral homes coordinate their services based on the preferences of the deceased and their families. They frequently handle essential administrative tasks, such as completing necessary paperwork, obtaining permits, coordinating with cemeteries, and submitting obituaries to news outlets. In the United States, there are several common types of funeral services. A traditional funeral service typically includes a viewing (sometimes referred to as a wake), a funeral ceremony held at the deceased's church or the mortuary chapel, and a graveside committal service. Direct cremation involves the mortuary receiving the deceased's remains, completing the required legal paperwork, and carrying out the cremation process. Direct or immediate burial occurs when the family opts to forgo a funeral ceremony and requests a prompt burial of their loved one. In cases where the deceased needs to be transported to or from another mortuary, the process involves preparing the body for shipment in a casket secured within an air tray or a combination unit. This is often necessary when the burial site is located in another state or country. When the deceased is brought to the funeral home, embalming may be performed to delay decomposition. The embalming process typically involves replacing the blood with a mixture of preservative chemicals and dyes, aspirating the internal organs, and setting the facial features of the deceased. Makeup is often applied to make the individual appear more lifelike. If the deceased has been disfigured due to an accident or illness, embalmers may use restorative techniques to make the body suitable for an open-casket service. If restoration is not possible or the family prefers, a closed-casket service can be arranged. Funeral homes often provide designated spaces for families to gather during visitations. These areas may include a viewing room where the deceased is displayed in their casket, allowing visitors to pay their respects. Funeral and memorial services may also be conducted at the funeral home. Many funeral homes offer prearrangement services, allowing individuals to plan their own funeral services in advance. With the growing popularity of cremation, more funeral homes now include on-site crematoriums. Those without such facilities often outsource cremation services to other providers. Some funeral homes are family-owned and operated, while others are part of larger corporate entities. However, corporate-owned funeral homes often present themselves as family-owned to maintain a personal and community-oriented image. One of the largest corporations in this industry is Service Corporation International. In popular culture, funeral homes have been depicted in various media. The television series Six Feet Under portrayed a fictional funeral home, while the series Family Plots showcased the operations of a real funeral home in California, running for two seasons before its cancellation. In the movie My Girl, the character Harry Sultenfuss (played by Dan Aykroyd) operated a mortuary from his home.
